subject: How can I hide reactive code that I need for ggvis from being displayed in rMarkdown

messages.author: 0366928fd06f3534
messages.subject: How can I hide reactive code that I need for ggvis from being displayed in rMarkdown
parts:
This a repeat of a question in the shiny discussion group but probably makes more sense here

I want to hide my code but echo=FALSE does not work for a reactive

```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

selectInput("category", "Choose Dataset:", c("mpg", "disp", "qsec"))

testCode <- max(mtcars$mpg)

# ggvis with dynamically changing columns
reactive({
  if (!is.null(input$category))
    col <- input$category
  else
    col <- "mpg"
  
  mtcars %>% ggvis(~mpg, ~disp)
  
}) %>% bind_shiny('foo')

ggvisOutput('foo')
```

The selectInput and ggvis chart show as required and the testCode line is hidden but I get 

## reactive({
##     if (!is.null(input$category)) 
##         col <- input$category
##     else col <- "mpg"
##     mtcars %>% ggvis(~mpg, ~disp)
## })

on the page , which is not desired

TIA

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] How can I hide reactive code that I need for ggvis from being displayed in rMarkdown
parts:
(cc Winston)

I think the problem here is that you have the ggvis() call inside the reactive and the bind_shiny() call outside of it. I think if you either move the ggvis call to be after the reactive, OR change "reactive" to "observe" and move bind_shiny('foo') to the inside, then the problem should be fixed.
